mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5% month-over-month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% MoM without subsequent tightening by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rises > 0.5% without subsequent negative market reaction.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 declines for 2 quarters without subsequent negative market reaction.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in one month signals a strong supply-side response, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increases > 2% MoM without subsequent positive market reaction.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, the combined signal of tight monetary policy and inflationary pressure leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combined condition is met without subsequent negative market reaction.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in one month signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increases > 300,000 without subsequent positive market reaction.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% month-over-month and real personal savings (RSAFS) increase by more than 5% month-over-month, the combined signal of reduced demand and increased savings leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combined condition is met without subsequent negative market reaction.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS remains below 2% without subsequent positive market reaction.
